intent: Accept the exact Diodes GBJ2510-F bridge as a reviewed alternate to Yangjie GBU2510A. Keep AC pins 2/3 unchanged, reverse only the DC endpoint mapping, enforce the package footprint identity, and use the same semantic mapping for PFC current injections without weakening the existing census checks.

requirements_completeness.scoped_result: R1 is addressed by the exact MPN/pin/footprint contract and shared PFC mapping. R2-R6 concern candidate bundles, native evidence, thermal comparison, and coordinator integration outside these three files; they were not evaluated as code findings here.

learnings.title: A net name is a claim, not an authority
learnings.note: The change correctly derives current semantics from an explicit reviewed pin map instead of inferring them from a net label.

learnings.title: Three-target verification ladder
learnings.note: Source graph and injection tests support code/model correctness; native footprint geometry and hardware applicability remain separate evidence rungs.

learnings.title: Claimed isolation versus actual connectivity
learnings.note: The topology mutation tests cross the semantic pin assignment boundary and reject a source that only changes the MPN.

residual_risks: The changed source/PFC contract does not itself prove the alternate footprint's native pad positions, UUIDs, or board geometry. The pending board/native work must provide that exact-ID evidence.
The existing thermal bridge-neck validator outside this scope is hard-coded to GBU2510A; an alternate GBJ candidate will remain blocked there until its reviewed native path is added.
No end-to-end pfc_power::run fixture exercises a GBJ source plus GBJ native board. The unit test covers the mapped injection graph, while candidate-native integration remains pending.
testing_gaps: Add or retain a source-bound GBJ native fixture test for pfc_power::run once the board agent supplies the exact footprint and native evidence.

coverage.simplify_review: All three ce-simplify-code rubrics were applied inline because repository instructions require sequential main-thread review and explicitly prohibit spawning children. No worthwhile reuse, quality, or efficiency finding was identified.
